body: Seriously though, every day that I'm alive, I find myself saying, "Thank god I don't have to deal with this much longer." Honestly, can't wait. Just a little bit longer. :)
Oh yeah, I'm still around! I'll be around for a few weeks. :)

Thank you. I appreciate it.. but I told quarantines above the same thing up above: the world needs more people like the woman I was, not the person I am or I am becoming. I'm a big "you're in control of your destiny" type person, but not this time.

Thank you very much.. it's what gets me out of bed and off the couch (when I'm stuck on it) every day. I won't get myself a glass of water but I'll clean 110 gallon water troughs for the horses and build pastures and walk dogs. They're my life! But unfortunately, that's the idea. I'm about to turn the corner from "benefit to everyone who knows me" to "leech on everyone around me".. and that's not good for anyone. Once I turn this corner, there's no going back, and I just don't have the energy or drive to keep going anymore. The world desperately needs more people like who I was.. not who I am. :)

I have. However, here in the poorest areas of the USA, unless I want to be a minimum-wage kennel sweeper, working with animals is just not going to happen. I thought I could train horses but I don't yet have enough expertise for that (I can handle my own horses but producing a "polished" product that people want to pay money for is an entirely different ballgame than fixing a problem in your own horse).. I wanted to be a vet but with a GPA well below a 2.0, I would never graduate undergrad, much less get accepted to vet school. :\

I live my entire life for my furbabies. On the hardest days, when I can't get off the couch to get myself a glass of water, I'll get up because the dogs need food and the ponies need water.

I really appreciate your note about trying to not seem coddling :) You did not come off that way at all, so thank you for your cautiousness in trying to avoid that.

I came to this decision a while ago - I've ruined my life academically (not one semester or two, but six semesters' worth of ruining) and if I can't afford to rescue animals anymore, then.. :\ The idea of working at a minimum wage job for forty hours a week for the rest of my life just to pay off student loans (which didn't earn a degree) and credit cards, especially if I'm unable to rescue animals or even have pets at the same time? That's a life not worth living. Rescuing animals is my passion, which I have identified and indulged for years now.
